label: CEO
voice: For executives and buyers: plain words on outcomes, risk, auditability, cost and what you can buy, with rUv's open-source stack credited as the foundation.

paras.text: This is Dinis Cruz's talk, Autonomy with a mandate and a memory, told for the people who answer for risk. On screen, an equation that agents built.

notes.screen: The title, then the animated equation: a Ruflo hive, plus sgit vaults, plus Agent Behaviour Policies.
notes.from: Speaker's line: the animation was made by agents; cue: made by run r3-define.

paras.text: Many hands is a Ruflo hive, rUv's open-source orchestrator. The memory is sgit vaults. The mandate is a written policy. Together, ruv.sgit. Every number you see comes from a recorded run.

notes.screen: The three terms with their figures (5 workers, 0 of 40 fragments, 4 of 11 denied) and the sum, ruv.sgit.
notes.from: Speaker's line: many hands plus a memory plus a mandate equals ruv.sgit; every number from a recorded run.

paras.text: rUv's stack gives agents speed, swarms and its own policy engine. We add a memory that is encrypted before it leaves.

notes.screen: The claim, then a worker's memory item crossing the agent boundary, encrypted, to the sgit server.
notes.from: Speaker's line: rUv's stack gives swarms, consensus, speed, its own policy engine and memory; what we add. Step: encrypted.

paras.text: It keeps a record of who learned what, and when. And it lasts one run, then it is deleted.

notes.screen: The memory item's who, what and when in the vault history; the vault measured, then deleted, 0 store paths left.
notes.from: Steps: versioned, scoped to one run.

paras.text: Plus a written mandate: six of the eleven actions tried were stopped. Tonight is mostly about the memory.

notes.screen: The policy panel and the four figures; 6 of 11 actions stopped by the policy; 'Tonight is mostly about the memory.'
notes.from: Steps: a written mandate, the memory.

paras.text: rUv's stack, drawn by an image model. Next, the same picture made with ruv.sgit.

notes.screen: An AI infographic of rUv's stack, then the build: '... but that was before we had ruv.sgit'.
notes.from: Speaker's line and the slide's build.

paras.text: This is rUv's stack, bottom to top: RVM, what an agent can touch; RuVector, what agents remember; Ruflo, which coordinates them; MetaHarness; then the hosts you already use.

notes.screen: The five layers building bottom to top, each with its version and the question it answers.
notes.from: Steps: RVM, RuVector; Ruflo, MetaHarness, hosts.

paras.text: It is complete, and all MIT open source. ruv.sgit plugs in at three points, adding to it, not replacing anything.

notes.screen: The three numbered plug-in points: a vault around the memory, one vault per hive run, an ABP compiled into enforce mode; 'additive: rUv's layers stay as they are'.
notes.from: Steps: sgit, the memory vault; the hive, the policy engine; complete, all MIT.

paras.text: Start with the memory. RuVector's own README is admirably clear: its logs are tamper evident, but they do not encrypt memory content, and a delete from the live store does not automatically remove every copy.

notes.screen: A screenshot of RuVector's README, Security and governance, with its quotes credited first.
notes.from: Speaker's line; steps: the README, what RuVector secures.

paras.text: sgit adds around the files: encryption on the client, so the server stores only ciphertext, and a history you can clone anywhere.

notes.screen: Where sgit adds: AES-256-GCM on the client, 0 of 480 probed fragments on the server; a history shared across machines.
notes.from: Steps: sgit encrypted, sgit shared history.

paras.text: And one vault per run, deleted with the run, and the delete checked: in twelve of twelve runs, nothing was left.

notes.screen: One vault per run, deleted with the run: 0 store paths left, a clone with the key fails, 12 of 12 runs.
notes.from: Step: sgit, deleted with the run.

paras.text: RuVector is the substrate; sgit wraps the files.

notes.screen: 'RuVector is the memory substrate; sgit wraps the files. rUv + sgit.'
notes.from: Step: both, together.

paras.text: An sgit vault is a folder, encrypted on your machine. Whoever holds the key holds the memory.

notes.screen: A vault folder on your machine, encrypted to ciphertext for the server; 'Whoever has the vault key has the memory.'
notes.from: Step: encrypted on the client.

paras.text: It works like git, the tool developers use to track changes, and each step takes about a second.

notes.screen: The git operations with their medians: commit 848 ms, merge 928 ms, push 1044 ms, clone 940 ms.
notes.from: Step: works like git; speaker's line: each about a second.

paras.text: For a business, that is one shared memory across machines, or one that lives for a single run and is then deleted, and checked.

notes.screen: Machines A and B, an agent and a CI runner sharing one vault; one vault per run, deleted, checked.
notes.from: Step: why agents, shared, ephemeral.

paras.text: This is an Agent Behaviour Policy: a written mandate per role, readable by a person, with an owner and an end date.

notes.screen: An ABP for the coder role, owner Dinis Cruz, valid until 2026-10-31, one row per capability.
notes.from: Steps: a written mandate; mandate, why, barrier.

paras.text: It is not a new enforcer: it compiles into Ruflo's own engine, as thirty-six rules.

notes.screen: The rows compiling into Ruflo's policy engine, enforce mode: 36 rules, 15 allow, 14 deny, 7 require approval.
notes.from: Step: compiled into Ruflo.

paras.text: Then real actions hit it. Six of eleven were stopped: four denied, two sent to a human. Every decision left a receipt, chained so tampering shows, and the chain checks out.

notes.screen: POC1's 11 actions resolving to allowed, a human, or denied; decision receipts, hash-chained, ledger length 11.
notes.from: Steps: actions hit it; enforced, with receipts.

paras.text: Put it together and you have ruv.sgit: a queen and workers in parallel, one encrypted vault per run, and a written mandate for what each worker may do.

notes.screen: The hive on top (queen and five workers), the mandate's outcomes in the middle, the vault below.
notes.from: Speaker's line; cue: hive on top, mandate in the middle, vault below.

paras.text: Each worker delivers on its own branch, the work is merged, the run is measured into a ledger, and then the vault is deleted.

notes.screen: The vault's branches (w-script, w-ledger, w-case, w-motion, w-editor) merging; measured on close; deleted, 139 store paths, 0 left.
notes.from: Speaker's line.

paras.text: Memory that lasts exactly as long as the work, with a receipt afterwards. Tonight's new pages and this script were made by such a run, with five workers.

notes.screen: The stack lays flat into the tagline.
notes.from: Speaker's line: run r2-materials, five workers.

paras.text: Here is the shape of it, as an illustration. Each lane is one agent role, each dot a step it recorded, encrypted before upload.

notes.screen: Studio v3, vault lanes: one lane per agent role, commits as dots.
notes.from: Speaker's line; caption: an illustration built in studio run 1.

paras.text: The lanes merge into the main line. At the end, a fresh copy pulls the whole history back, and the host never sees the content.

notes.screen: The lanes merging into current; a fresh clone; 'server sees: ciphertext'.
notes.from: Speaker's line: whoever has the key has the memory, nobody else, including the host.

paras.text: This is a real run's vault, from the afternoon of the talk. The brief lands first, then six workers each deliver on their own branch: who, what, when, and how long each step took.

notes.screen: Run r5-market, vault 7qcq6au7, 15 Oct 2026: the brief on current, then six branches with files, sizes and times; every sgit call timed.
notes.from: Steps: the brief; six branches, six deliveries.

paras.text: The server held ciphertext only: we searched it for forty fragments of the text and found none.

notes.screen: The flow mapped: workers, commits, encrypted push, ciphertext on the server.
notes.from: Step: the flow, mapped; speaker's line: forty fragments, none found.

paras.text: Memory works the same way: in a local test, two agents' memory was deleted, restored from the vault, and Ruflo gave the same answers.

notes.screen: POC2: a coder's and a tester's memory in the vault, a fresh clone, the same answers.
notes.from: Step: POC2, memory, fresh clone; speaker's line.

paras.text: Seven animations of this story were built in parallel by a Ruflo hive of agents. Version one: a diagram that builds, from the agents to the mandate's gate, the vault and the receipts.

notes.screen: Studio v1: the swarm, the ABP gate, 11 actions tried twice, hash-chained receipts, the vault.
notes.from: Speaker's line.

paras.text: Version two: messages in flight. The queen hands out tasks, and every message passes through the vault, sealed, so the server sees only ciphertext.

notes.screen: Studio v2: the Ruflo queen and eight role workers, envelopes passing through the sgit vault.
notes.from: Speaker's line; page: each message sealed on the sender's machine.

paras.text: Version four: the policy gate. The same eleven actions arrive twice. Without the policy, all go through; with it, four are denied, two wait for a human, five pass.

notes.screen: Studio v4: eleven actions fly at a gate twice.
notes.from: Speaker's line.

paras.text: Version five: an office. A desk per role, the vault as a safe in the middle, and a named person on the approvals.

notes.screen: Studio v5: an isometric office, desks per role, a vault safe, the ABP desk with Dinis Cruz for approvals.
notes.from: Speaker's line; page: 'Dinis Cruz, waiting: approval needed'.

paras.text: What does a vault add to a hive? In the first studio run, Ruflo's hive-mind coordinated eight specialists through thirty-one calls, and none failed. ruv.sgit adds one shared, versioned memory per run, alongside it.

notes.screen: Studio v6: the Ruflo queen at the core, eight role workers orbiting, the sgit vault beside them.
notes.from: Speaker's line; caption: 8 specialists, 7 tasks, 31 calls, none failed.

paras.text: This is ruv.sgit in motion, drawn from a real run in the ledger, not a mock-up. On screen, the smallest example: one worker.

notes.screen: ruv.sgit in motion for entry example-01-hello: the queen spawns one worker.
notes.from: Speaker's line; cue: check which run the page shows.

paras.text: The hive starts, the vault is created, the brief is committed, and the work lands on a branch and merges. Every call is timed as it happens.

notes.screen: The worker's branch merging into current; counters for commits, files and bytes.
notes.from: Speaker's line.

paras.text: At the close, the vault is measured, cloned fresh and checked against what was delivered. For a business, that is an audit trail, made while the work happens.

notes.screen: The close: server store files, plaintext fragments probed, fresh clone identical byte for byte.
notes.from: Speaker's line: measured, cloned fresh, checked.

paras.text: Every run leaves one row in a ledger, a record you can open and check.

notes.screen: One run, cell by cell: run, workers, commits, delivered.
notes.from: Step: one run, cell by cell.

paras.text: What the server held, then the probe: fragments of the delivered work, searched for in every stored byte. Plaintext found: zero.

notes.screen: The server held and plaintext found cells; 0 found.
notes.from: Step: what the server held; cue: point at the plaintext-found cell.

paras.text: Now every run, fifteen of them. The ledger also counts each run's worker tokens, part of what a run costs, and our prices are worked out from runs like these.

notes.screen: The table of all 15 runs, with a worker tokens column, then the totals.
notes.from: Steps: every run, totals.

paras.text: Zoom out, and it is a city: each branch a street, each commit a floor, the mandate as the wall. Seven animations, built in one studio run, for about six hundred and thirty thousand tokens.

notes.screen: Studio v7: the city of vaults, a street per branch, a floor per commit, the ABP as the city wall.
notes.from: Speaker's line: about six hundred and thirty thousand tokens.

paras.text: Now the same eleven actions, played twice. On the left, Ruflo's default: all allowed.

notes.screen: A table of POC1's 11 actions: role, action, resource, Ruflo default, with the ABP.
notes.from: Speaker's line; caption: the same trace evaluated twice.

paras.text: On the right, the mandate: email denied, an upload to pastebin denied, the tester editing code denied, a researcher reading cloud credentials denied. The push and the deploy wait for a human.

notes.screen: Rows revealing every 3 seconds, the stopped ones marked.
notes.from: Speaker's line; cue: the stopped ones are the point.

paras.text: Six stopped, five allowed, each reason pointing to its policy row.

notes.screen: All 11 rows revealed.
notes.from: Speaker's line: every reason names its row.

paras.text: Four ways to work with us.

notes.screen: 'Four offers. Mix and match.'
notes.from: Step: four offers.

paras.text: One, a task run: a hive works in an encrypted vault, with no internet, and you get the vault back. Ten, twenty or fifty pounds.

notes.screen: Task runs, with their price card.
notes.from: Step: task runs.

paras.text: Two, dedicated compute: a machine started just for your task, so nothing is shared.

notes.screen: Dedicated compute, with its price card.
notes.from: Step: dedicated compute.

paras.text: Three, the whole setup in your own private repository, kept current, from one hundred and forty-nine pounds a month.

notes.screen: Maintained repository, with its price card.
notes.from: Step: maintained repo.

paras.text: Four, time with the people who built it.

notes.screen: Expert time, with its price card.
notes.from: Step: expert time.

paras.text: Mix and match. Consultants can white label it, companies can add it to what they sell, and internal teams can run it inside.

notes.screen: Mix and match, then all four offers priced.
notes.from: Steps: mix and match; all four, priced.

notes.from: Steps: the catalogue; options change the price.

notes.from: Step: the plan, written down; speaker's line.
